feed.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?

entry.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
entry.summary:
A new section has been added to the Bitcoin information page, providing a clear explanation of both bc1q and bc1p address types. Gem is configured to receive transactions on bc1q addresses and is capable of sending funds to any standard Bitcoin address type, including bc1p. This update enhances user understanding by outlining the compatibility and flexibility in transaction processing.
To assist users who encounter errors such as “invalid address” when interacting with bc1p addresses, a concise guide has been prepared. This resource offers step-by-step instructions and troubleshooting tips for resolving address validation issues. The guide can be accessed at [Gem Wallet’s documentation](https://docs.gemwallet.com/blockchains/bitcoin/bitcoin-address-types-bc1q-and-bc1p), serving as a practical reference for both customers and support teams.
Additionally, comprehensive educational content regarding Taproot and its implications for Bitcoin addresses is now linked within the guide. The resource at [whentaproot.org](https://whentaproot.org) provides in-depth insights into Taproot, enabling support personnel to direct users to authoritative information about address formats and their respective benefits.
Clear explanations of the advantages associated with various address types have also been incorporated, equipping users with the rationale behind selecting one address format over another. This approach ensures that users are informed not only about technical compatibility but also about the underlying reasons for choosing specific Bitcoin address types.
